1.explanation: The core of this bug lives in the render-blocking-resources audit implementation. That file gathers all CSS and JS resources that delay first paint, but doesn’t filter out file:// URLs. To fix the issue, you need to update lighthouse-core/audits/byte-efficiency/render-blocking-resources.js so that any resource whose URL starts with the file: protocol is skipped and not included in the list of render-blocking items.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse runs its “Eliminate render-blocking resources” audit on a page that includes <link> or <script> tags pointing at file:/// URLs, it still treats those local file:// resources as if they were real network requests and reports them under “render-blocking resources” with non-zero wasted time—even though file:// never actually blocks network rendering. In other words, the audit fails to ignore file-scheme URLs and incorrectly flags them as performance problems.

2.explanation: The file lighthouse-core/audits/byte-efficiency/render-blocking-resources.js contains the logic to identify and report CSS/JS files that block initial rendering. It iterates over network records and currently does not exclude file:// schemes, so those local resources end up in the audit. Modifying this audit to skip resources whose URL protocol is file:// (similar to how data: URIs are excluded) will prevent local file URLs from being flagged as render-blocking.
2.bug_scenario: When auditing an HTTP-served page that includes <link> or <script> tags pointing to file:/// URLs, Lighthouse’s “Eliminate render-blocking resources” audit still flags those local file:// resources (transfer size 0 KiB) as blocking the first paint and reports hundreds of wasted milliseconds—even though file:// URLs never go over the network and can’t block rendering.
